I found a problem using it on MacOs (I'm using an intel based Mac x86_64 but I'm assuming the problem would also happen with arm Macs).

This is the mrp, just a scene with a control with this script:
```
extends Control

func _ready() -> void:
	Input.joy_connection_changed.connect(on_joyconnection_changed)
	
func on_joyconnection_changed(joy_id:int, connection_status:bool):
	if connection_status:
		# On connection I'm setting the joystick to player id p2 (int 1)
		Input.set_joy_player_id(joy_id, PLAYER_ID_P2)
		print("Joy connected %d set to player id %d" % [joy_id, Input.get_joy_player_id(joy_id) as int])

func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event is InputEventJoypadMotion:
		# On unhandled input whenever there's joy motion I'm printing the event player id, I expect it to be int 1 (PLAYER_ID_P2), but it's 0. If I take the device id and I get the player id from input I can verify the player id is not 0.
		print("Joypad motion device id %d event player id is %d player id retrieve from joystick is %d" % [event.device, event.player, Input.get_joy_player_id(event.device) as int])
```

Essentially the player id is not being set on the Input Event when I'm on Mac. On Linux and windows it works as intended, seems to be a Mac-only issue.

I further investigated the macOS issue.

For a while I thought maybe it wasn't calling set_player_from_device() in input_event.cpp but I found out that it actually is calling it.

I added a print_line debug to set_player_from_device where it's handling `InputEventJoyButton` and `InputEventJoyMotion`:
```cpp
		print_line(vformat("This is a valid joypad thing for device local %d from event %d player local %d player from event %d from input %d from iterator %d", device, event->get_device(), player, event->get_player(), input->get_joy_player_id(device), E->value.player_id));
```
I also added a print inside the `if (!E)` to see if maybe the iterator was invalid for some reason. That print did not print so the event is valid.

This is what gets printed:

```
This is a valid joypad thing for device local 0 from event 0 player local 0 player from event 0 from input 1 from iterator 0
```

So if I call `input->get_joy_player_id(device)` it finds the correct number. But the iterator that is trying to find the Input::Joypad with the device number seems to find an incorrect joypad and returns a wrong number.

So in the end I changed that section of the `set_player_from_device` to the following and it fixed the issue, but I don't know if it's worse for performance or something:
```cpp
// Joypad events.

	Ref<InputEventJoypadButton> jb = event;
	Ref<InputEventJoypadMotion> jm = event;
	if (jb.is_valid() || jm.is_valid()) {
		Input *input = Input::get_singleton();
		if (!input->_get_joy_names().has(device)) {
			player = PlayerId::P1;
			return;
		}
		player = input->get_joy_player_id(device);
	}
```

Personally, I think this is a great feature that could be generalized beyond just the concept of "players". For example, it could be used to easily swap between different sets of controls in a single player game.

There's also the fact that the `PlayerID` enum only goes up to 8 players. I've seen local multiplayer stuff in the past that could go up to 32 players, so I don't think it makes sense to set an arbitrary limit here. It also doesn't really need to be an enum, since what it describes is purely numeric.

So I think that instead of a `PlayerID` enum, control sets should be indexed by int or StringName.

@Mickeon thank you so much for the feedback!
Yes, I agree that most of the content of this PR are quality-of-life improvements.
But as you also correctly noticed, the implementation is still very correlated to previous iteration with the UI features.

In fact, I think that this PR should be the starting point to achieve these other local multiplayer capabilities that are currently missing or very cumbersome to implement.
The first things that come to my mind:
- UI local multiplayer support
- Easily swappable input maps (for each player)

As we previously discussed here and on rocket chat, anyone of these would complicate the PR too much.

So, as a result, I think that this PR should be designed to be as flexible as possible, so that any support for local multiplayer later can be added on top of it.

If you and anyone interested agree with this, we can eventually come up with a list of local multiplayer features that we may want to support later in the engine, so that we can design this PR and its API so that it's compatible with each one, and hence be a great starting point.

Is something like that already available in some proposals? We can also look at previous issues and proposals to accomplish this, if that's interesting for anyone.

From the comments I get that this PR differentiates between players by filtering the input events with the PlayerID.
I think a better system would be to have the ability to have one set of input events per PlayerID (or bit if using bitmasks):

- It would solve the issue of sharing a device.
- Also make it possible to rebind actions by player (so player 1 can jump with A and player 2 can jump with Y).
- It would be possible to use multiple devices for one player.
- And it would fit better with the systems that are already in place.

To resolve the problem of how to create one set of input events for each player, I would make actions have a "generates multiplayer input events" flag that makes it so the engine duplicates the default input events with the correct device, a number of times determined by a project setting.

Also changing the order of devices through a script could be done with a function to batch swap the input events of all actions of one player with another.

Great initiative, lots of good ideas here. Looks like the work is progressing at a good pace. :)

I would like to propose a possibly better way to handle the Input mapping UI in the project settings, sorry if this is outside the scope of this PR though, but it seems like this would be a good place to attach the ideas. I tend to think of Input as two parts - actions, and devices. I believe this is the model godot use as well... Albeit in a quite rough form.

So, why not formalize this split? Instead of project settings taking up a single column where actions are defined and inputs are assigned almost as an afterthought...

**What if**, actions are grouped in a column to the left, with an added checkbox, let's call it "PlayerUnique". On the right, you have an array list of inputs per action. Now, let's say you have a game with four inputs per player, and two global actions, the setup for a Keyboard would look something like this (Action - Props - Bindings):

* **quit** - PlayerUnique[ ] - [Escape, Backspace]
* **pause** - PlayerUnique[ ] - [T, Enter]
* **left** - PlayerUnique[x] - [A, LeftArrow]
* **right** - PlayerUnique[x] - [D, RightArrow]
* **jump** - PlayerUnique[x] - [W, UpArrow]
* **attack** - PlayerUnique[x] - [LeftControl, RightControl]

Expected behavior:

* Player1 may use W, A, D, LeftControl to control their character, T to pause the game, and Esc to quit the game (shutdown)
* Player2 may use arrow keys and RightControl to control their character, Enter to pause the game, and Backspace to quit the game (shutdown)

So quit and pause are both linked to the same action regardless of which player presses it, while the other actions are assigned to a specific player.

Also worth noting: There are games that do split a gamepad (Switch Joycons are the prime example here - one gamepad, effectively two controllers). I also seem to recall a Playstation 2 or 3 game from the late 00s a friend told me about, where you controlled one character with the left side of the controller and another with the right. Beating the game alone was next to impossible, it was a great couples game IIRC :)

Of course, this idea might have already been investigated and discarded, if so, thank you for hearing me out and my apologies. :)

Unfortunately this is very unlikely to be merged soon.
Reasonably, Godot mantainers want to better refine the design of the implementation, since it would be a new "layer" to mantain for them.
The discussion is in a stale WIP state if you follow the thread on RocketChat.

I currently don't have much time to work on this.
Even though I still plan to bring this forward, note that a lot of things have to be redesigned and implemented, so it will be a matter of months if not years to be merged officially, considering the agreement process for new "big" features.

This seems rough but it's just to be clear with you if you plan to wait for a feature like this for your current projects.
You can either use this or the other PR that also implements multiplayer for Control nodes in the meantime (they should be in a workable state).
But if you want a full-fledged officially supported solution for multiplayer games you should probably look elsewhere for now...
